# gitmoap_provider_submission (Data Source)

Get a provider submission. The submission's state, its manifest, who submitted it and when, the outcome of the checks on its images, and the reviewer's decision and notes once it has been reviewed. Only the publisher that made it and platform administrators may read it.

The token needs `provider_publishing:read`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "submission_id" {
  type = string
}

data "gitmoap_provider_submission" "example" {
  submission_id = var.submission_id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `submission_id` (String) Submission id

### Read-Only

- `attest_result` (Attributes) The result of checking a community or private provider's images, by capability. The images stay
in your registry; nothing is copied or signed. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--attest_result))
- `auth_schema` (String) JSON: set it with `jsonencode()`.
- `manifest` (Attributes) One published version of a provider, with the capabilities it offers. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--manifest))
- `manifest_digest` (String)
- `mirror_result` (Attributes) The result of copying a verified provider's images into gitmoap's registry, by capability. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--mirror_result))
- `owning_group_id` (String)
- `provider_description` (String)
- `provider_id` (String)
- `provider_name` (String) The provider's name, as the catalog shows it.
- `published_at` (String)
- `publisher_id` (String)
- `registry_pull_secret_ref` (String)
- `review_notes` (String)
- `reviewed_at` (String)
- `reviewer` (Attributes) Who did something — a person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — with what a
client needs to draw and link them, so a page of records names its actors without a lookup each. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--reviewer))
- `source_image_refs` (Attributes Map) Each capability's image in your registry, by capability id. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--source_image_refs))
- `state` (String) Where a provider submission stands, from review through to publication or refusal.
- `submitted_at` (String)
- `submitted_by` (Attributes) Who did something — a person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — with what a
client needs to draw and link them, so a page of records names its actors without a lookup each. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--submitted_by))
- `target_tier` (String) How a pipeline provider is distributed and how much it is vouched for.
- `version` (String)

<a id="nestedatt--manifest"></a>
### Nested Schema for `manifest`

Read-Only:

- `changelog` (String)
- `contract_version` (Number)
- `cosign_signature_ref` (String) Where the cosign signature is stored in the registry, when the images are signed.
- `lifecycle_state` (String) Lifecycle state of a published `ProviderVersionManifest`. `Active` is the
default; `Deprecated` still runs but the trigger-time validator surfaces a
warning; `Sunset` runs only inside its grace window, after which a trigger
referencing it fails validation.
- `manifest_capabilities` (Attributes List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--manifest--manifest_capabilities))
- `manifest_digest` (String) The SHA-256 digest of the version's `gitmoap-provider.yaml`. May be empty.
- `provider_id` (String)
- `published_at` (String)
- `published_by` (String) `"platform"` for platform-authored providers; a publisher id otherwise.
- `signed` (Boolean) Whether the version's images are signed with gitmoap's cosign key, as verified and
platform providers' are.
- `sunset_at` (String) When the version was sunset. Set only for a sunset version.
- `sunset_enforced_at` (String) When the sunset's grace period ends. After it, a run that uses the version fails to start.
- `version` (String)

<a id="nestedatt--manifest--manifest_capabilities"></a>
### Nested Schema for `manifest.manifest_capabilities`

Read-Only:

- `bindable` (List of String) Config keys that can take their value from an earlier step. Each has an optional `value`
input port of the same name: connect it and read it with `{"$from": "<key>"}`, or leave it
unconnected and write the value yourself.
- `cache_enabled` (Boolean)
- `capability_id` (String)
- `config_schema` (String) The JSON Schema a step's `config` must satisfy to use this capability.

JSON: set it with `jsonencode()`.
- `default_timeout_seconds` (Number)
- `description` (String)
- `image_digest` (String) The exact build of the capability's container image, when the catalog records one. Pinned so
a run cannot pick up a different build behind the same tag.
- `image_uri` (String) The container image that runs the capability, with an immutable version tag.
- `input_groups` (Attributes List) Rules about which inputs are alternatives to each other. Empty for most capabilities. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--manifest--manifest_capabilities--input_groups))
- `inputs` (Attributes List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--manifest--manifest_capabilities--inputs))
- `name` (String)
- `outputs` (Attributes List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--manifest--manifest_capabilities--outputs))
- `requires_docker` (Boolean)
- `source_image_ref` (String) For a verified provider, the image's location in its publisher's registry before gitmoap
copied it. Absent for providers gitmoap builds itself.
- `stage_type` (String) The pipeline stage a capability belongs to. Maps verbatim to the
`stage_type` field of a capability in `gitmoap-provider.yaml`.

<a id="nestedatt--manifest--manifest_capabilities--input_groups"></a>
### Nested Schema for `manifest.manifest_capabilities.input_groups`

Read-Only:

- `description` (String) Why these ports constrain each other, in the provider's own words. Rendered beside the
group, and repeated in the validation error when the group is unsatisfied — which is the
point: the sentence explaining the rule reaches the person who broke it.
- `kind` (String) How many of a group's ports may be connected.
- `ports` (List of String) The member input ports, in the order the author should read them.


<a id="nestedatt--manifest--manifest_capabilities--inputs"></a>
### Nested Schema for `manifest.manifest_capabilities.inputs`

Read-Only:

- `cardinality` (String) How many connections an input port accepts: `one` (the default) or `many`, in which case the
step waits for every connected source. An output can always feed any number of inputs.
- `description` (String) What this port is for, in the provider's own words. Absent on a few older providers.
- `name` (String)
- `port_type` (String) What kind of data a port carries. Two ports connect only when their types match.
- `required` (Boolean)
- `schema_id` (String)

- `cardinality` (String) How many connections an input port accepts: `one` (the default) or `many`, in which case the
step waits for every connected source. An output can always feed any number of inputs.
- `description` (String) What this port is for, in the provider's own words. Absent on a few older providers.

- `port_type` (String) What kind of data a port carries. Two ports connect only when their types match.

<a id="nestedatt--reviewer"></a>
### Nested Schema for `reviewer`

Read-Only:

- `avatar_url` (String) The principal's picture, when one is known. Absent otherwise: a client derives the
deterministic avatar URL itself.
- `email` (String) The principal's address. An agent's is a generated no-reply address — the author of its
commits. `unknown` on a deleted actor and empty on a redacted one.
- `id` (String) The principal's id: a user id, a service account id or an agent id, as `kind` says. Empty on
a redacted actor.
- `kind` (String) A person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — which of the three a principal is,
and so which page it links to: a person's profile, a service account's page or an agent's page.
- `username` (String) The name to show: a person's or service account's username, or an agent's handle (which
always ends in `-ai`). `deleted-user` when the actor no longer resolves, `redacted` when the
caller may not see who it was. A closed account whose work stays is `closed-` and twelve hex
digits, a shape no open account may take, with an address under `.invalid`.
